text: Grouping by service pointed at Azure Kubernetes Service. Drilling into the node pool, kubectl get hpa shows ten replicas running, with CPU utilization at only twenty-two percent against a seventy percent scale-up target.

The autoscaler isn't broken -- it's doing exactly what it's configured to do. minReplicas is set to ten, and two weeks of real p95 utilization data confirms two replicas would comfortably cover real traffic, even at peak hours.

The root cause traces back to Terraform's Lesson Four setup. Driftwood's module repo keeps a standard profile, at two minimum and six maximum replicas, and a peak-season profile, at ten minimum and twenty maximum, reserved for scheduled high-traffic events.

The engineer wiring up the autoscaler referenced the peak-season profile instead of standard, most likely copied from a different, higher-traffic environment's configuration. Ten replicas is a valid setting -- just for the wrong environment.

Because roughly two to three pods fit on one node, ten idle replicas keep about three extra nodes running around the clock -- the biggest piece of the gap between the seventeen-fifty projection and the twenty-four sixty forecast. Next lesson picks up a second, unrelated finding on the AWS side.
